title: Adaptive kernel profiling and compilation tuning for MHA/GQA/MoE onboarding
creator: Aria Patel
description:
Problem: New model onboarding has regressed in token throughput and tail latency for non-standard attention blocks (GQA) and sparse routing (MoE). We need a repeatable per-model pipeline that produces a published performance profile and a pinned compilation artifact (kernel choices + tuning flags) that the serving runtime can select at deploy time.

Goal: Deliver an end-to-end flow that takes a model checkpoint -> per-architecture kernel selection matrix -> tuned compilation profile -> published performance profile in the model catalog, with CI checks and a fallback policy. Scope covers MHA variants, GQA, and MoE layers for the initial tranche of community and customer models.
acceptance_criteria: A1: For each model type (MHA, GQA, MoE) generate a compilation profile that includes kernel choices, tiling parameters, and quantization knobs committed to model metadata.
A2: Published performance profile shows median throughput and p95 latency for two representative input shapes and batch sizes in the catalog UI and is retrievable via API.
A3: Runtime automatically picks the pinned profile during rollout; when profile is unavailable, runtime falls back to the generic 'safe' kernel set without crashing.
A4: CI job validates new onboarding profiles by running a synthetic perf harness and failing the pipeline if latency regressions >10% or errors appear.
A5: Documentation and runbook for adding new models and re-tuning existing profiles are in Confluence with step-by-step commands and required metrics.
A6: Benchmarks for at least 3 onboarding models (one MHA-heavy, one GQA-enabled, one MoE sparse) show >=5% improvement in cost-per-token vs generic profile or match baseline latency with lower cost.
plan: Task 1: Add kernel-selection stage to onboarding pipeline that probes available kernels for each op type and records microbenchmarks.
Task 2: Extend compilation step to accept per-op tuning parameters (tile sizes, vector widths, use_fp16/quant flags) and persist compiled artifact hash.
Task 3: Build a small search heuristic (greedy + hillclimb) tuned per-architecture to reduce tuning time for MoE routing kernels and GQA fused ops.
Task 4: Integrate CI perf checks and a 'publish profile' step that writes performance metadata to the model catalog service and marks the model version as pinned to the profile.
Task 5: Create runtime selection logic to prefer pinned profile by model_version; implement a healthcheck that re-measures a sample during first N minutes of rollout.
Task 6: Write docs, runbook, and a one-hour workshop for solutions engineers on interpreting profiles and re-tuning
decisions: Decision 1: Use a two-stage tuning approach: (a) short microbenchmarks to prune kernel candidates, (b) targeted hillclimb on remaining candidates. This balances cost and coverage.
Decision 2: For MoE we will prioritize routing throughput and memory footprint over raw kernel FLOPs because expert activation patterns drive real-world performance.

Decision 3: Quantization profiles will be generated but not auto-applied; they will be tagged as 'suggested' in the catalog and require explicit opt-in at deployment time to avoid silent quality regressions.
Decision 4: Store compiled artifacts in artifact store keyed by model_version+profile_hash. Runtime will fall back to a canonical 'safe' profile if artifact missing.
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting with runtime, compiler, and onboarding teams. Agreed on acceptance criteria and shortlist of three onboarding models.
2026-02-24: Prototype microbenchmark harness implemented (github PR #3842). Initial MHA microbenchmarks revealed 12-18% variance across kernels for 2048-seq shapes.
2026-03-02: Greedy pruning implemented. For GQA fused attention the fused-kernel performed worse on small batch sizes; we added batch-size conditional selection.
2026-03-07: MoE routing kernel tuning discovered two tiling configurations that improve p95 by ~9% for a 64-expert model on A100. Marcus verified memory stability.
2026-03-10: Integrated publish-to-catalog step to write performance_profile JSON. Running full CI bench on pipeline; seeing flaky test in CI harness (investigating seed instability).
rollback_plan: If a published profile causes regressions in canary: immediately unpin model_version via catalog API and switch runtime to 'safe' profile for that model_version.
If compiled artifact is corrupt: purge artifact store entry and trigger auto-recompile with previous known-good profile hash.
If CI tuning job repeatedly flakes: disable auto-publish and require manual review for next 24 hours while investigation completes.
notes_risks: Risk: Tuning cost for MoE models can be high due to expert count and activation sparsity. Mitigation: limit search budget and cache results across similar topologies.

Risk: Differences between local perf harness and production host (driver versions, MIG/SM partitioning) can yield mismatches. Mitigation: add a production-representative validation stage in Dedicated environment.
Note: We intentionally avoid auto-applying quantization to preserve model quality; a separate QC pipeline will evaluate quality drop vs. cost savings.
